slots.title: U.S. session recap — Sept. 18, 2026
slots.body:
U.S. indexes split on Sept. 18.
The S&P 500 rose +0.1% to 7,646.04 (+8.28 pts).
The Nasdaq Composite gained +0.4% to 26,522.55 (+104.25 pts).
The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell −0.2% to 51,682.64 (−95.40 pts).
The Russell 2000 lost −0.5% to 2,860.40.

The CBOE Volatility Index fell −4.1% to 14.81, with an intraday range of 14.80–15.63.
Coverage tied the calendar to triple witching — simultaneous expiry of index options and futures — after a choppy week; the Wall Street Journal described a quiet finish to that stretch.

Sector performance on Nasdaq sorted cleanly.
Technology led at +1.5% average change.
Financial services followed at +1.2%.
Communication services was weakest at −2.3%.
Utilities averaged −1.5%, energy −1.6%, and industrials −0.9%.

Megacap and liquid large-cap moves carried the narrative.
Netflix fell −4.7% to $71.79.
PepsiCo dropped −2.9% to $129.75, with a session low at its 52-week low of $129.55 in the data.
Microsoft slipped −0.8% to $493.78.
On the upside, Broadcom rose +3.0% to $357.61, ASML +3.1% to $1,679.92, NVIDIA +1.3% to $222.27, and Taiwan Semiconductor +1.0% to $434.67.

The earnings calendar in the feed carried no major after-the-bell reports for this recap.
The economic diary included Baker Hughes U.S. oil rig count at 452 versus 450 prior and 451 estimated, plus late CFTC positioning releases (including S&P 500 speculative net positions at −100.5K vs −76.0K prior).

Energy equities softened with the sector average −1.6%.
Brent crude settled at $103.87 (−0.9%).
The United States Oil Fund (USO proxy in the tape) closed at $153.82 (−1.0%).

Gold futures (GCUSD) rose +0.6% to $4,424.90.
The dollar proxy UUP was flat at $28.39 (0.0%).
EUR/USD held near 1.15 (+0.1% in the feed).
Bitcoin (BTCUSD) added +0.5% to $81,295.73.

Treasury snapshot dated Sept. 16 in the data showed the 10-year yield at 5.0% and the 2s10s spread at 0.27 percentage point.

Overseas benchmarks from the same bundle: Japan’s Nikkei 225 +1.4% to 65,018.95; FTSE 100 −0.3%; Hang Seng +0.1%.
The session headline mix — inflation and geopolitical worry versus AI-related strength in tech — matched the index split at the U.S. close.
